w: At 5.05 pm, Swamishri landed at Kuwait International Airport. Swamishri and sadhus were welcomed by Dr. Mukesh Delwadiya, Harish Derasari and other devotees.

During the evening assembly Swamishri blessed the devotees, saying, "Inner peace cannot be attained through a predominance of mundane affairs. By prioritizing satsang in one's life one finds peace of mind... The human birth and this satsang is priceless. We have this human body, but through satsang and the God-communion sadhu one comes to understand how to use it to attain moksha..."

Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha rituals of the canvas murtis of Shri Akshar Prurushottam Maharaj and the Guru Parampara for the renovated Hari mandir in the township of Shankartekari in Jamnagar city.
At 10. 55 a.m. Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals in the Swaminarayan hari mandir in the suburb of Kapadiyanagar, Mahuva.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the assembly hall for his puja. The sadhus and youths sang kirtans suited to the day. At the end, Krishnapriya Swami was singing a kirtan. The kirtan "Bhakti tana jya pur umatya" (Where floods of devotion surged) was being sung to a rising beat. Meanwhile Swamishri came down from the side stage onto the main stage, went close to the devotees and gave darshan to everyone. The atmosphere was surging with devotion, and meanwhile, right next to the sadhus keeping the beat, Jaydeep Swadiya's little child Deep was striking the tabla as if he were not in this world at all! Nodding his head, dancing as he sat, throwing up both his hands, he was rhythmically striking the tabla. Swamishri kept looking at him for quite a while. This is in fact a daily routine, but today he was on the tabla. Watching with a gentle smile, Swamishri suddenly gestured to the cameraman Kunal Bhavsar and said, "Film this too!"

Swamishri drew away the camera, which was usually focused only on Swamishri, and had it turned towards the little child. Swamishri can show such large heartedness that even a small child gets importance.

The kirtan "Bhakti tana jya pur umatya" (Where floods of devotion surged) was being sung at a rising tempo. Meanwhile, Swamishri came down from the side stage onto the main stage and went close to the devotees, giving darshan to everyone. There was a surge of devotion in the atmosphere, and meanwhile, right next to the sants keeping the rhythm, Jaydeep Swadiya's little child Deep was striking the tabla as if he were not in this world at all! Shaking his head, dancing as he sat, tossing up both hands, he was striking the tabla in rhythm. Swamishri kept looking at him for a long time. This is actually a daily routine, but today he was on the tabla. Smiling gently as he watched, Swamishri suddenly gestured to Kunal Bhavsar, the cameraman, and said, "Film him too!"

Swamishri drew away the camera, which normally hovers only on Swamishri, and had it turned towards the little child. Swamishri can show such large hearted friendliness that even a small child receives importance.

Mahant Swami Maharaj had darshan of the guru parampara in the Abhishek Mandapam. In the room of sanctified items, Atmaswarupdas Swami asked, "Every day you step down from the mat spread out and go closer on this side for darshan. Whose darshan are you having?"
Swamishri said, "Of the sanctified items of Bhagatji Maharaj."

Because a pillar got in the way of the darshan of these sanctified items, Swamishri used to go closer there. This gave a special glimpse of how, when he has darshan, he does so filling his heart with all the memories.
